title: ETL pipelines & system integrations
subtitle: Keeping disparate enterprise systems in sync with a pragmatic, reusable approach
overview: I built a set of data synchronization pipelines to stop fragile, one-off integrations from slowing the business down. Instead of hammering together bespoke scripts each time, I created reusable client libraries and a small configurable ETL engine so new integrations are reliable and repeatable.
challenge: HR, ERP, process automation and PIM lived in separate systems (SuccessFactors, NetSuite, ARIS, a custom PIM). Each new data flow meant rewriting glue code and risking production. That made launches slow and operational support painful.
solution: I split the problem into three practical layers: small, reusable service clients; a transformation engine driven by a simple Expr-based configuration; and an orchestration layer that runs and monitors pipelines. Each piece is versioned and tested independently so teams can add a connector without touching everything else.

keyAchievements.title: Near-real-time sync
keyAchievements.description: Delivered a SuccessFactors ↔ ARIS sync that reduced stale data windows from hours to minutes. It runs as a Kubernetes cron job and tolerates transient failures.

keyAchievements.title: Config-driven field mapping
keyAchievements.description: Built an Expr-based mapping format so product managers can tweak field rules without a deploy. It supports computed fields and conditional transforms.

keyAchievements.title: Reusable client libraries
keyAchievements.description: Implemented small Go clients for NetSuite, ARIS and the internal PIM so new pipelines start from working code instead of a blank file.

keyAchievements.title: Production reliability
keyAchievements.description: Added retry logic, validation checks and clear observability so failures surface promptly and recover automatically where safe.

keyAchievements.title: Scalable architecture
keyAchievements.description: Designed the pipeline to run many syncs in parallel without cross-contamination and to make backfills and ad-hoc exports straightforward.

learnings: Treat integrations as products: they need releases, tests and clear ownership.
Configuration beats copy-paste. Giving non-developers safe knobs (mapping rules) saves time and reduces risk.
Good observability turns noisy support tickets into quick rollbacks and targeted fixes.
Small, well-tested client libraries dramatically shorten onboarding for new connectors.
